intro: Comparing two things with más, menos and tan, and the special forms mejor, peor, mayor and menor.
p.más.consejo: It has an accent so it is not mixed up with «mas» (but). With «que» it compares: «más grande que».
p.menos.consejo: It is the opposite of «más»: «menos caro que». It does not change gender or number.
p.tan.consejo: It goes before an adjective and is completed with «como»: «tan alta como Pablo». It does not change.
p.que.consejo: After «más» or «menos» you write «que»: «más grande que Granada». It has no accent.
p.como.consejo: After «tan» you write «como»: «tan alto como yo». It has no accent.
p.grande.consejo: It works for masculine and feminine: «un café grande», «una ciudad grande». Plural: «grandes».
p.caro.consejo: It changes with the noun: «caro», «cara», «caros», «caras». It is the opposite of «barato».
p.barato.consejo: It changes with the noun: «barato», «barata». It is the opposite of «caro».
p.bueno.consejo: Before a masculine noun it loses the -o: «un buen café». Its comparative is «mejor».
p.malo.consejo: Like «bueno», before a masculine noun it loses the -o: «un mal café». Its comparative is «peor».
p.mejor.consejo: It is the comparative of «bueno». You do not say «más bueno» or «más mejor». It works for masculine and feminine.
p.peor.consejo: It is the comparative of «malo». The normal form is «peor», not «más malo»: «es peor que ayer».
p.mayor.consejo: With people it compares age: «mi hermana es mayor que yo». After «que» comes «yo», not «mí».
p.menor.consejo: It is the opposite of «mayor»: «mi hermano es menor que yo». It works for masculine and feminine.
b1.texto:
To compare two things there are three patterns:

- **más + adjective + que**: Madrid es **más grande que** Granada.
- **menos + adjective + que**: Granada es **menos cara que** Madrid.
- **tan + adjective + como**: Ana es **tan alta como** Pablo.

Four adjectives have their own form and do not use «más»: **mejor** (from «bueno»), **peor** (from «malo»), **mayor** and **menor** (age). You do not say «más bueno» or «más mejor».

After **que** and **como** come **yo** and **tú**, not «mí» or «ti»: mi hermana es mayor que **yo**.
b2.f1.texto: Granada is less expensive than Madrid.
b2.f2.texto: My sister is older than me.
b2.f3.texto: This coffee is as good as the other one.
b2.f4.texto: The coffee in Granada is better than the one in Madrid.
b2.f5.texto: The one in Madrid is not worse.
b2.f6.texto: My brother is younger than me.
b2.f7.texto: You are as tall as your sister.
b4.titulo: Más, menos, tan and the special forms
b4.texto:
With adjectives:

- más grande **que** / menos caro **que**
- tan alto **como**

With verbs, no adjective: Ana trabaja **más que** yo; Pablo gana **menos que** ella.

Own forms:

- bueno → **mejor** (el café es mejor que el té)
- malo → **peor** (este día es peor que ayer)
- big or older → **mayor** (mi hermana es mayor que yo)
- small or younger → **menor** (mi hermano es menor que yo)

**Mejor, peor, mayor** and **menor** do not change between masculine and feminine. Plural: mejores, peores, mayores, menores.
b4.e1.texto: This house is as expensive as that one.
b5.f0.texto: The village up high is smaller than the one in the valley.
b5.f1.texto: Its white houses look older than the rocks along the path.
b5.f2.texto: The morning air is as fresh as the water of the river.
b5.f3.texto: A girl runs across the square less quickly than her dog.
b5.f4.texto: The sky seems bigger from here.
b5.f5.texto: In the valley, the market is bigger than the village square.
b5.f6.texto: The sellers shout louder than the birds by the river.
b5.f7.texto: The coffee at the market smells better than freshly baked bread.
b5.f8.texto: Pablo drinks his coffee as slowly as a cat.
b5.f9.texto: Under the moon, the village up high seems bigger than ever.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Muy» does not compare two things: it only says «very».
b7.o0: Este café es mejor que el otro.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Mejor que» says that one beats the other.
b7.o1: Este café es peor que el otro.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Peor que» says that one loses to the other.
b7.o2: Este café es tan bueno como el otro.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is it! «Tan… como» says they are equal.
b7.pregunta: Which sentence says two things are equal?
b8.frase: Granada es menos cara que Madrid
b8.traduccion: Granada is less expensive than Madrid
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Tan… como» makes the two people equal.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Tanto» is used with verbs or nouns; before an adjective use «tan».
b9.pregunta: Which word compares two equal things?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «My sister is older than me.»
b11.o0: Mi hermana es mayor que mí.
b11.o0.refuerzo: After «que» it is not «mí»: it is «yo».
b11.o1: Mi hermana es mayor que yo.
b11.o2: Mi hermana es más mejor que yo.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Mejor» already means «more good». It takes no «más».
b12.frase: Este café es ____ que el otro.
b12.o1.refuerzo: You do not say it like that: «bueno» has its own form, «mejor».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Mejor» already compares. It does not need «más».
p.casas.consejo: Same word as «casa» in the singular. The -s makes it plural.
p.antiguas.consejo: The gu before a sounds like «gwa». The stress falls on TI.
p.rocas.consejo: The r at the start is strong, like «rr». The c before a sounds like a «k».
p.deprisa.consejo: Made from «de» and «prisa», hurry. Say de-PRI-sa, stress on PRI.
